branch: in-flight pulse (.tool-line.run::before / .think-live::before) raised at content_block_start, settled by tool_result, web_search_tool_result, or the turn ending
provenance: Every frame SHAPE here is reused from fixtures whose provenance is already established — content_block_start/delta/stop for tool_use is fixture 40's sequence, the `user` tool_result is fixture 07's, `result` is fixture 44's real 2026-08-12 capture (CLI 2.1.228), `__transcript` is fixture 08's, and server_tool_use/web_search_tool_result ride the same machinery per docs/client-parity.md item 12. NOTHING new is claimed about what the CLI emits. What is new is only what the RENDERER must do with those shapes, which is what is asserted. Each independent scenario opens with __clear rather than inheriting the previous one's DOM: fixture 44's lesson is that two states which can mask each other must each start from a known baseline, or an assertion reads as satisfied when nothing set it. The animationName assertions are the half that pins the CSS — a class-count assertion alone passes even if the stylesheet never attached. STEPS 15-19 ADDED 2026-08-13 after the first version shipped a real bug while green: every earlier step builds its tool line directly in #log, because nothing on the WIRE creates a .turn-body — the real panel only makes one when the user sends (addUserMessage -> newTurn). So the paint containment that .turn-body carries was never in the picture, and it was clipping the ring into a cut half-rectangle in the actual panel. Those steps use the harness's `setup` hook to build the turn the way the panel does, then send the same wire frames into it. They are KEPT after the halo was dropped for a plain fade: they now pin the opposite property — that the in-flight dot grows outside nothing, so containment stays on and the clipping class of bug cannot come back unnoticed. STEPS 20-26 ADDED 2026-08-13 from a MEASURED session (~/.claude/projects/-home-syncroze-Sites-claude-brains-testing/8a0b1939-ceaa-415e-9e6e-895e2e1b7803.jsonl): an Agent tool_use at 16:55:53.309Z received its tool_result at 16:55:55.158Z reading 'Async agent launched successfully … The agent is working in the background.' — the ack text here is that record verbatim. The task_started/task_progress/task_updated/task_notification shapes are the ones probed on CLI 2.1.222 and documented above taskLine() in chat.html; they are LIVE-ONLY and appear in no transcript, so they cannot be re-measured from disk. STEPS 27-31 ADDED 2026-08-13 from session 06c02917-268d-408d-aec3-9beff7a0ec23: the user asked for three dummy sub-agents with one failing, and the failing one still rendered green. Measured answer — the persisted notification for it reads <status>completed</status> with a <result> ending 'Status: FAILED', and the sub-agent's OWN transcript holds the is_error:true tool_result. So the CLI considers the agent completed and the failure lives one level down; the green dot was right. The real gap those steps close is that `failed`/`killed` would ALSO have rendered green, because a sub-agent's tool_result is only ever the launch ack. The status vocabulary is `<status>completed|failed|killed</status>`, read verbatim out of the 2.1.228 binary with `strings`. A sub-task status DOT was built on 2026-08-13 and REMOVED the same day, with its __agent_outcome round trip and its Kotlin scanner: whether a sub-agent's work failure leaves any structured trace turns out to depend on how the agent ran the command — a foreground failure lands as an errored tool_result, the same command pushed to run_in_background by the sandbox guard leaves none — so the dot rendered red or green for the same task between two runs. The .t-prog assertions that remain are about its `run` CLASS only, which is colour-only and predates all of this.
